column1: # Capability taxonomy — the input to tools/capability_count.py
# group <TAB> capability <TAB> regex pattern (case-insensitive, matched against page body)
# This is a STARTING taxonomy for a customer-engagement platform, written before the
# corpus was read. It is deliberately generic. Revise it after the first index pass,
# when you can see the vendor's own vocabulary — a vendor's product names are the
# highest-signal patterns and you cannot guess them.
# Rules that keep the count honest:
#   - one capability per row; overlapping patterns are fine, counts are independent
#   - prefer \b word boundaries; "sms" without them matches inside other words
#   - a product NAME is worth more than a category word. Add them as you find them.
#   - when you change a pattern, rerun and note the change — a number that moved
#     because the pattern moved is not a finding.
# The starter patterns above the line were category words written before the corpus
# existed. This revision replaces them with BRAZE'S OWN PRODUCT NAMES wherever one
# exists, because a product name is a far higher-signal pattern than a category word.
# Numbers moved between the two runs BECAUSE THE PATTERN SET MOVED, not because the
# product changed — recorded in docs/FACTS.md "Numbers that were wrong and are now
# right" and never to be read as a finding.
